headword: {大口真神|おおくちのまかみ}
gloss: wolf deity; messenger of the mountain gods

definitions.explanation: A wolf revered in Shinto folklore as a guardian spirit and messenger of the mountain gods. Now-extinct Japanese wolves ({日本狼|にほんおおかみ}) were worshipped under this name at shrines believed to protect crops from wild boar and deer.

examples.japanese: {大口真神|おおくちのまかみ}をまつる。
⟦{三峯|みつみね}→三峯：30953_mitsumine⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大口真神|おおくちのまかみ}をまつることで{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Mitsumine Shrine is known for enshrining the wolf deity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{村人|むらびと}→村人：13062_murabito⟧たちは{大口真神|おおくちのまかみ}のおふだを⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧にはった。
examples.english: The villagers put a talisman of the wolf deity at the entrance of the house.

notes:
{大口真神|おおくちのまかみ} (literally "great-mouthed true god") is a title for the {日本狼|にほんおおかみ} (Japanese wolf) worshipped as a protective spirit and messenger of the mountain gods (⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧).

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Shrines such as ⟦{三峯|みつみね}→三峯：30953_mitsumine⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧ (Saitama) and {武蔵御嶽|むさしみたけ}⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧ (Tokyo) issue wolf-deity talismans (おふだ) said to ward off fire, thieves, and crop-raiding animals.
- The Japanese wolf went extinct around 1905, but the cult persists at these mountain shrines.
- Related word: ⟦{狼|おおかみ}→狼：04334_ookami⟧, which explains the wolf's broader cultural symbolism.
